findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the pandoc timeout reaps the whole process GROUP (not just the direct child) by invoking pandoc via Popen(start_new_session=True) + the existing shared rebar._proc.reap_process_group, OR justify in the plan how pypandoc's internal subprocess reaps a pipe-holding grandchild — otherwise the timeout fires while a spinning pandoc survives (bug d843).
evidence: Plan: 'wrap every pandoc invocation with a per-call wall-clock timeout'
Plan Context hazard: 'one corpus body drove pandoc's jira reader to spin 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc invokes pandoc with no timeout'

acli_subprocess.py:38-42: 'subprocess.run(timeout=) only reaps the DIRECT child — a grandchild on the pipe defeats it (CPython bpo-30154). So we Popen(start_new_session=True) … reap the whole process GROUP'
rebar._proc.reap_process_group EXISTS (shared, stdlib-only leaf) and is importable from jira_family without violating ADR-0035 (no adapters/jira import)
findings.finding: The plan's timeout mechanism ('wrap every pandoc invocation with a per-call wall-clock timeout') will not reliably kill the hang it names: a per-field pandoc spin at 95.8% CPU is precisely the pipe-holding-grandchild case where subprocess.run(timeout=)/pypandoc's internal subprocess timeout only reaps the direct child and the CPU-spinning process survives (repo bug d843; acli_subprocess.py:35-45; CPython bpo-30154). The repo already ships the fix as the shared leaf rebar._proc.reap_process_group (Popen(start_new_session=True) + SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain), reused by the ACLI transport and grounding harness, but the plan neither requires process-group reaping nor reuses it.
findings.location: Approach → 'Hard timeout + verbatim fallback'; Scope → adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py; AC line 1
scenarios: Pathological jira-reader input makes pandoc spin at ~95% CPU with a grandchild holding the capture pipe; the wall-clock timeout expires but the process is never killed, so the reconcile still stalls.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach and Scope, state that wiki_render invokes pandoc directly with subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) and reaps on timeout via rebar._proc.reap_process_group(grace/drain), mirroring acli_subprocess, rather than relying on pypandoc's timeout-less convert_text; add an AC that a spin-forever synthetic input is reaped (process group killed), not merely abandoned.

findings.finding: The plan asserts a per-invocation wall-clock timeout on pandoc as its core new capability but does not name the mechanism, while its own Context concedes 'pypandoc invokes pandoc with no timeout' — pypandoc's standard convert API accepts no timeout parameter, so the timeout wrapper's integration path (e.g., invoke the wheel-bundled pandoc binary directly via subprocess.run(timeout=) after locating it, plus reliable child/process-group kill) is unspecified.

findings.finding: Batching bounds spawn count but the plan states no upper bound on batch size (units-per-invocation or bytes-per-invocation). An unbounded batch trades one hazard (spawn tax) for another: a single large batch that times out degrades many units at once, and a very large combined body could itself be slow or memory-heavy.

scenarios: A changed body with 40 safe units is batched into one invocation; healthy conversion takes longer than the fixed per-call timeout, so all 40 units false-positive-degrade to verbatim Markdown.
